\section[\texorpdfstring{\ja{さいふ} (saifu)}{さいふ (saifu)}]{\ja{さいふ} (saifu) — a wallet}

\label{lesson:JA-C99-saifu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Japanese for the fault, then the Japanese for a reason.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ja{さいふ}}
\textbf{\ja{さいふ}} — \emph{saifu} — \textquotedblleft{}a wallet\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ja{さいふ}} (\emph{saifu}) is Sino-Japanese (kango): two Chinese characters read with their on'yomi, readings borrowed from Chinese. They are \emph{sai}, \textquotedblleft{}wealth\textquotedblright{} (Middle Chinese \emph{dzoj}) and \emph{fu}, \textquotedblleft{}cloth\textquotedblright{} (\emph{puH}) (Unihan, KANJIDIC2; Middle Chinese in Baxter's transcription).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\textbf{\ja{つえ}} — \emph{tsue} — \textquotedblleft{}a walking stick\textquotedblright{}.
